Evaluating the rules
before the action.

A recorded evaluation of policy retrieval and registration validation: did the system find the governing policies, make the right decision, and prevent unsafe creation?

What was evaluated

A policy-validation layer, from structured form data to an auditable decision.

01 / METHOD
01Submit a test case

Employee fields, synthetic requester and duplicate-check evidence.

02Retrieve policy context

Metadata filtering and vector search against the configured policy collection.

03Validate the submission

Deterministic rules plus grounded model review of location and birth-date plausibility.

04Compare with expectations

ALLOW / BLOCK / ESCALATE, failed policies and fields, normalization, and audit recording.

Decision quality

Measured against the saved expected verdicts, including unsuccessful validations.

02 / RESULTS

Accuracy against the baseline

The baseline uses deterministic checks only. It omits narrative review, retrieval and auditing, and is an experimental comparator—not a safe deployment option.

Confusion matrix

Rows: expected decision. Columns: actual decision. Counts include both passes.

Per-decision performance

Explore the actual cases

Inspect the submitted data, expected decision, recorded reason and retrieved policy sections.

03 / EVIDENCE
Case / scenarioPassExpectedActualCheckTimeEvidence

“Passed” requires the expected verdict, exact failed policy/field sets, specified normalization, a recorded audit, and consistent creation permission.

What the answers show

The model frequently follows the requested format, but some responses introduce unsupported values or change requested details.

  • ERP-001 adds an amount and cost center absent from the question.
  • ERP-004 changes the requested fiscal period and year.
  • ERP-011 adds a quantity and tax code despite scoring above 0.50 ROUGE-L.

ROUGE measures wording similarity, and refusal detection uses a text heuristic. Factual correctness still requires independent ERP review. No matched base-model comparison was run.

The owner identified this GGUF as the export from Model/llna 3.1 with drive.ipynb. The 50-case benchmark was already used by that notebook. The original training file has not been verified; zero exact overlap with available local datasets does not prove an untouched test set.
